tagline: The world's first and largest Bitcoin Treasury Company
hero_kpi_rationale: MSTR's positioning and value are anchored in its massive Bitcoin treasury, which defines its financial strategy and market identity. The scale of its Bitcoin holdings directly impacts shareholder value and fundamentally differentiates it from all other technology companies.

kpis.name: Annual Bitcoin Purchases
kpis.explanation: Dollar amount of bitcoin purchased during the fiscal year.
kpis.description: The company purchased $22.47 billion of bitcoin in 2025, compared to $22.07 billion in 2024, funded through convertible debt and preferred stock issuances.
kpis.signal: Sustained massive BTC purchases in 2025: +$22.47 billion

kpis.name: Total Bitcoin Holdings
kpis.explanation: Total number of bitcoins held by the company in its treasury.
kpis.description: Total holdings reached 672,500 bitcoins as of December 31, 2025, up from 447,470 BTC at the end of 2024, representing a 50.3% increase.
kpis.signal: Massive accumulation: 672,500 BTC as of end-2025

kpis.short: Net Cash Used in Operating Activities
kpis.name: Net Cash Used in Operating Activities
kpis.explanation: Amount of cash spent by the company's core operating activities.
kpis.description: Cash used in operations increased by $14.2 million in 2025 due to a higher net loss and the transition to subscription-based revenue (deferred billing, accrued commissions).
kpis.signal: Deterioration in operating cash flow in 2025

kpis.short: Net Cash Provided by Financing Activities
kpis.name: Net Cash Provided by Financing Activities
kpis.explanation: Cash raised through equity, debt, or other financial instruments.
kpis.description: The company raised $24.8 billion through convertible notes, preferred stock, and common stock issuances, an increase of $2.71 billion versus 2024.
kpis.signal: Strong financing activity via preferred instruments in 2025

kpis.name: Preferred Stock Issuance
kpis.explanation: Amount raised through issuance of preferred stock (IPO and ATM).
kpis.description: The company raised $6.92 billion in 2025 through the initial issuance of five classes of preferred stock (STRF, STRC, STRE, STRK, STRD), establishing a new capital channel.
kpis.signal: Innovative new financing vehicle launched in 2025

kpis.name: Dividends Paid on Preferred Stock
kpis.explanation: Total amount of dividends paid to preferred stockholders.
kpis.description: In 2025, the company paid $381.4 million in dividends across its five classes of preferred stock (STRF: $86.8M, STRC: $122.1M, STRE: $12.0M, STRK: $87.8M, STRD: $72.7M).
kpis.signal: First year of preferred dividend payments

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Difference between revenue and cost of goods sold, expressed as a percentage.
kpis.description: Estimated at 75%, in line with enterprise software companies, reflecting the software analytics business model.
kpis.signal: Typical margin for enterprise software vendors

kpis.name: AI Software Leadership
kpis.explanation: Leadership position in AI-driven enterprise analytics software.
kpis.description: The company positions itself as an industry leader in AI-powered enterprise analytics software, under the 'Intelligence Everywhere' vision.

kpis.name: Annual Bitcoin Purchases
kpis.explanation: Dollar amount of bitcoin purchased each year.
kpis.description: In 2025, the company purchased $22.47 billion of bitcoin, compared to $22.07 billion in 2024, maintaining an aggressive accumulation strategy.

kpis.name: Preferred Stock Issuance
kpis.explanation: Amount raised through issuance of preferred stock.
kpis.description: The company raised $6.92 billion in 2025 through the initial issuance of five classes of preferred stock, creating an innovative 'digital credit' instrument.
kpis.signal: Innovative new financing vehicle launched in 2025

kpis.name: Total Bitcoin Holdings Growth
kpis.explanation: Year-over-year increase in the number of bitcoins held.
kpis.description: The company accumulated an additional 225,030 bitcoins in 2025, increasing from 447,470 to 672,500 BTC, a 50.3% growth.

risks.title: Extreme volatility of the bitcoin price
risks.score_rationale: The risk is central in the document, repeatedly mentioned with strong language ("significant volatility", "may not be able to sell"). The company holds 717k bitcoins, indicating massive exposure. The Capital category is highly weighted here.

risks.title: Dependence on fundraising to purchase bitcoin
risks.score_rationale: A key point in the 10-K: the company relies on equity and securities issuances to fund its bitcoin purchases. The language affirms the continuity of this model. An existential risk if capital markets close.

risks.title: Risk of bitcoin market manipulation
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly cited with concerning language ("subject to fraud and manipulation"). The market is described as immature and vulnerable. High weighting for Litigation risk in an uncertain regulatory environment.

risks.title: Future regulation of bitcoin
risks.score_rationale: Although not detailed here, the risk is implicit in the nature of the bitcoin market ("developing regulatory landscape"). Restrictive regulation could limit liquidity or usability.

risks.title: Concentration of risk on a single asset
risks.score_rationale: The company allocates a massive portion of its treasury to bitcoin, a non-diversified asset. Repeated mentions of significant exposure. Capital category with maximum intensity.

risks.title: Dependence on innovative financial instruments
risks.score_rationale: The company issues 'digital credit' and other complex instruments. The filing notes there is "no assurance" they will remain available or successful. Cautious language but high risk of failure.

risks.title: Liquidity risk in bitcoin sales
risks.score_rationale: Explicit mention that the company "may not be able to sell" its bitcoins at market prices. The market is described as having "limited liquidity". Combined operational and credit risk.

ai_positioning.summary: The company MSTR does not mention artificial intelligence or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F filing.
